HushThreads v0.0.16 has 20 patches for Threads 452.0.0.50.64 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so you need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer. Update Threads to 452 before you patch.

Hide ads now also goes after the ads Threads fetches for the replies under an opened post. There's a new `Disable swipe to Search` patch too, for accounts where a sideways swipe on the feed slides into Search.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#12](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/12) found ads among the replies when you open a post. Those come with the post rather than through the feed, and Hide ads now empties that list as well.
- [#13](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/13) asked for a way to stop the feed sliding into Search on a sideways swipe. Turn on `No swipe into Search` on the Feed page and restart Threads. The Search button still works.

## Threads

- HushThreads now patches Threads 452.0.0.50.64 only, the newest stable version, and drops 451.0.0.51.80. Update Threads to 452 before you patch. The bundle is built with Morphe's 2.0 patcher, so you'll need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer.
- Hide ads now also takes out the ads that show up among the replies when you open a post. Threads sends those with the post instead of through your feed, which is how they slipped past before. Turn Hide ads off, or pause HushThreads, and they show the way Threads draws them. The Hide ads switch says so in all six languages.
- New `Disable swipe to Search` patch. On accounts where a sideways swipe on your feed slides into Search, the swipe stops and your feed stays put. The Search button still opens Search. Only some accounts have the swipe, and on the others nothing changes. The `No swipe into Search` switch is on the Feed page of HushThreads settings and starts off. Restart Threads after you flip it.
- A download that runs out of its ten minutes now always says it was too slow. Every so often its last wait ended a fraction of a millisecond early, and you were told the network failed instead.

## Tooling

- A release can't go public until the whole app is walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk` and stops before the tag or GitHub if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Threads crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` does that walk. It patches Threads from the release bundle and installs it, opens the feed, Search, Activity, a profile and a post by their links, then goes in through the Profile tab, the profile's Settings button and the HushThreads row in Threads' settings and opens every HushThreads settings page. A screen only counts when Threads shows that screen's own view, since a link Threads doesn't handle still opens Threads, on the feed. Any Threads crash or ANR since the walk began fails it, and the receipt it writes is the one publish asks for. Its only taps are those three steps and the settings rows, each checked on its own screen, so it can't follow, block or message anyone, or like a post.

## Update

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.0.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.16 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
2. Get Threads 452.0.0.50.64 (arm64-v8a, version code 512207626) and patch that. v0.0.15 was the last release for Threads 451.
3. Manager's default selection has every patch except `Change version code`, `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates`. Turn on Expert mode if you want any of those.
4. Patch with the Morphe Manager signing key you used last time. That's what lets the update install over your patched Threads and keep your data and your login. Coming from the stock Threads, uninstall it first.
5. On a fresh install, sign in with your Instagram username and password.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Threads APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads#install).

## Validation

1004 runtime tests and 287 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints and the release script checks. All 20 patches applied without forcing to Threads 452.0.0.50.64, and the release receipt records the run. The dependency advisory check passed.

HushThreads v0.0.15 has 19 patches for Threads 451.0.0.51.80 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so you need Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer.

Copy text is back on opened posts, and Open links in browser now catches ad links and lead form links too. Settings got Quick setups for changing several switches in one tap, a Report a problem row that fills in your versions for you, and they stay open now when Threads redraws itself. Saving photos and videos got a lot of fixes, the biggest one for phones with smaller screens, where Save photo saved nothing.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#9](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/9) found that Copy text didn't do anything on an opened post. Pressing and holding the post's text brings up Copy text again, and the new `Copy text on long press` switch under Posts turns it on or off.
- [HushFacebook#146](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushFacebook/issues/146) asked for a way to keep HushThreads settings out of the menu you get by holding Threads' icon. The new `Settings shortcut on the app icon` switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page does that, and the Threads logo still opens settings with a long press.

## Threads

- Don't want HushThreads settings in the menu you get by holding Threads' icon? Turn off the new `Settings shortcut on the app icon` switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page and it leaves that menu right away, while Threads' own shortcuts stay. A long press on the Threads logo and the HushThreads row in Threads' settings still open the settings, and Pause leaves the switch as you set it.
- Pressing and holding the text of an opened post brings up Copy text again, the same as in your feed, so you get the whole post with its links. It had stopped doing anything on 451. A new `Copy text on long press` switch under Posts in HushThreads settings turns this on or off. It starts on and comes with every build.
- Open links in browser now also covers the places on 451 that used to skip it. An ad's link button and a swipe up on an ad in the media viewer send the ad's web link to your browser the same way post links go, and so do the privacy policy and disclaimer links on a lead form. Meta's own pages still open in Threads.
- Search's Follow suggestions row is gone too. It has its own switch, `Hide follow suggestions in Search`, right under Hide suggested users on the Feed page, and it starts on. Nothing takes the row's place, and search results and topics stay as they are. Turn the switch off, or pause HushThreads, and Search looks the way Threads draws it.
- Save photo and Save all work on phones with smaller screens again. On a 720 px wide screen Threads only keeps a photo at up to 750 px, and HushThreads took every one of those for a thumbnail and saved nothing. It now saves the largest copy there is, still prefers a full size one when Threads has it, and still never saves an avatar-sized copy.
- Disable video autoplay now also tells Threads' video prefetcher to hold off. The switch only held a feed video at its cover frame, so Threads could still start downloading a held video ahead of time. The patch now answers the prefetcher's autoplay-off question itself, only where the prefetcher asks it, so Instagram's older autoplay checker is left alone. With the switch off, paused or in safe mode, Threads' own answer goes back as before. Checked on a Galaxy S22 with Threads 451. The prefetcher got the hold answer with the switch on and Threads' own with it off, and a tapped video still played full screen.
- The HushThreads settings home page has two new rows. `Quick setups` changes a set of switches in one tap: Quiet hides ads and suggested accounts, Privacy stops most usage reports, takes tracking off shared links and hides your screenshots from Threads, and Back to defaults puts every feature switch back. A toast says how many changed. `Report a problem` opens a new GitHub bug report with your HushThreads and Threads versions, your phone and the switches you have on already filled in.
- More settings is now a heading on the HushThreads settings home page, with Appearance, Links, Updates, Set when you patched, Pause, backup and diagnostics and About listed under it. Every page is one tap from home and Back always goes home. Report a problem and Support HushThreads are still the last two rows, and the patch descriptions and bug report form point to the shorter paths.
- Don't use Quick setups? Press and hold its row on the settings home page and it's gone, and its help line says so. To bring it back, tap the Quick setups row on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page. Screen readers get the same press and hold on that row, and no other row offers one.
- HushThreads settings stay open when Threads redraws itself, after you change the font size or switch dark theme from the quick settings, or when Android closes Threads in the background and you come back. They used to close. They now come back on the page you were on. That holds with the settings open over two Threads screens and one of them closed, and on Android 9 in split screen when the Threads side sits for more than 30 seconds before you tap back into it.
- A settings file you pick for Import or Export isn't lost anymore when Threads redraws itself while the file picker is open, after a font size or dark theme change, or when Android closes Threads in the background to make room. The settings came back as if you hadn't picked anything. The file picker now opens through a small invisible screen of HushThreads' own, which keeps your pick until the settings are back. Access to the file ends once it's read or written. If Android closes Threads before that, it ends the next time Threads starts. Two quick taps on Import or Export open one picker, not two.
- After an export or import, the Export settings or Import settings row says how it went, in full, until you run another. That message used to show only in a pop-up, and newer Android versions cut those off after two lines, so a refusal like a damaged file lost its "Nothing was changed."
- Save's messages are short enough to read whole on Android 12 and later, which cut a message after two lines. On an S22 the proxy message stopped mid-word, and the slow-download one was just as long. A carousel's result now shows each line as its own message, so a line under the counts, like a proxy asking for a password, isn't lost. The German, Spanish, Indonesian, Portuguese and Turkish wording was shortened to fit too.
- A download that only trickles in now stops after ten minutes per file and says it was too slow, instead of holding one of the three save slots for as long as the server likes. A host lookup that never answers gives up after 20 seconds, and Cancel now ends a save that's still waiting on one.
- Cancel and the download time limit now end a save even when the phone's proxy service stops answering. Waiting proxy calls share the fixed limit on background network checks, so repeated attempts can't keep creating threads.
- A save's download now has a connection of its own that never asks Threads' cookie store or sign-in prompts for anything, so it can't send a cookie or a password, and it drops every cookie a server or a redirect sets. It still goes through the proxy your Wi-Fi or phone settings name and checks the server's certificate the same way. If that proxy asks for a password, the save stops and tells you, since it never sends one.
- On Android 9, a save without Threads' Storage permission now stops before it downloads anything and tells you where to turn the permission on. A carousel stops fetching its remaining pages if the permission is taken away partway through.
- Joining the picture and sound of a VP9 save (or AV1 before Android 14) now stops before it would take more than 24 MB of memory, and the save falls back to the single file. A file built from millions of tiny parts can't run Threads out of memory that way anymore. Cancel is also noticed while the join is still reading the tracks.
- When a save finds no picture or video it can keep, the diagnostics report now lists the kind and size of every address it looked at, so a bug report shows why. It never includes the addresses themselves.
- When the regular Instagram app from Meta sits beside your patched Threads, the Links page in HushThreads settings says Instagram won't open Threads posts or profiles here. That's Instagram's own check, and it's why Instagram says it couldn't load the website.
- When the settings list can't be put on the HushThreads screen at all, the screen shows Retry and Back instead of staying blank. Retry opens the page you were headed to, with your switches as you left them.
- When Threads rebuilds its screen with the settings open (after a text size change, say, or when Android closed Threads in the background), a settings page that fails to come back now gives way to a fresh page. Before, that failure would have crashed Threads, since it happens where the settings' own Retry and Back can't catch it.
- TalkBack now reads the Threads logo at the top of the feed as "Threads". Before, it stopped on the refresh spinner inside the logo and said "Progress bar". The README also says the logo ignores taps and holds while the feed loads or refreshes.
- TalkBack no longer stops on the HushThreads settings list as a whole to offer a long press that does nothing there. Quick setups, the one row with a long press, still offers it.
- HushThreads now keeps a note of how each switch starts in the build you patched. When a later build changes how a switch starts, one you never changed keeps the setting it had. Earlier builds left no such note, so this starts working with the update after this one.
- Settings file access stays tracked when a disk write or Android's permission service fails. Cleanup retries after a restart, and retrying the same file can't keep lasting access without a saved cleanup record.
- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Threads was patched with, not just a short summary. For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of the changelog, and the description was a paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's Threads bullets after the summary. You'll see it from the next release on.

## Tooling

- A GitHub description that names no release, patch count or Threads build now passes the release facts check and stays as written when a release publishes. Both used to refuse it, though a description like that has nothing a release can leave out of date. One that names any of those is still held to this release's and rewritten as before.
- The release cut now moves the release check test's User-Agent from whatever version it names. The v0.0.14 prep left that test on 0.0.13, so the next cut found nothing to move and stopped.
- The file picker behind Export settings and Import settings now has its own entry in the source ledger. Its two classes never had one, so the provenance test failed on every full run since they were added.
- When the final APK check catches the direct browser hook overwriting something Threads still needs, it now says which case it found. The register can be past the method's own locals, or Threads reads it right where the hook goes in, or Threads reads it once the link has opened. Each test build has to fail for its own reason, so one that trips the wrong part of the check doesn't pass anymore.
- Save's contract tests now cover the two other ways into Copy link's row call that would skip the Save row, a switch case and an exception handler aimed straight at it. The patch and the final APK check already refused both, but only a plain jump had a test, so losing either refusal would have gone unnoticed.
- The final APK check now holds Disable video autoplay's prefetch hold to its contract. Where Threads' prefetcher asks Instagram's autoplay-off question, the answer has to go through the extension right after it's read and come back in the same register, and every jump to the test that reads it has to pass through that call too. Nothing else may make the call. The question itself, its Olympus twin, Instagram's older autoplay checker and the prefetch dispatcher have to stay as Threads wrote them, and a build without the patch leaves every one of them alone. Each rule has a test build that only it refuses.
- The final APK check's browser guard has a test build only its completion half can catch: a link hook on a register that's free where the hook goes in but read again once the link has opened. No test build failed that half alone before, so losing it would have gone unnoticed.
- Save's final APK contract got stricter. A branch inside the post menu's Copy link case that jumps straight to the row call would skip the Save row, so the patch and the check both refuse one now. Share's jump onto Copy link's row still works. Every static method on the media bridge class has to be a bridge the patch writes, and written, so one left empty or one the patch doesn't know fails. A build without Save has every bridge and the activity reader checked as shipped, and a changed menu is reported at the first instruction that differs.
- The final APK check now holds Save photos and videos to its own contract. The post menu's Copy link path has to carry exactly one Save row, drawn with the calls Copy link's own row is built from and handed the menu and its composer, while every other menu item still reaches Copy link as before. The row's readers, its click and all fifteen media bridges have to point where the patch found them. A build without Save has to leave the menu and every stub as they shipped, and a bundle from before Save had a status reads as leaving it out.
- The build classpath inventory refuses to write when a project's buildscript graph is missing, instead of quietly leaving it out. That happens when a build doesn't evaluate every project, as under configure-on-demand, and the refusal names each one. Its Guava probe also stopped failing every Gradle command when it can't find one of the two plugins. It records no jar for that plugin now, and only the inventory refuses. A refused run also deletes the previous inventory, so nothing reads an old one as this run's.
- The same classpath now resolves commons-lang3 3.18.0 instead of the 3.16.0 the Morphe plugin asks for, which is inside GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v (CVE-2025-48924, 3.0 to 3.17.0). That was the last advisory OSV reported for the build's 114 plugin components, and the build advisory gate now finds none. It's a floor too, so it goes quiet once the plugin asks for 3.18.0 or later.
- The classpath the build plugins run from now resolves Guava 33.7.2-jre instead of 33.5.0-jre, which is inside GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94 (CVE-2026-102554, 4.0 to 33.7.1). It's a floor, so a plugin that later asks for a newer Guava still gets it. The build classpath inventory also records which jar the Morphe and Android Gradle plugins really load the advisory's three classes from, and it refuses to write when that isn't the Guava the classpath resolved. The bundle build and the focused registry tests pass with it.
- The source census now waits out a rate limit for as long as the answer says. GitLab throttles unauthenticated reads and answers 429 with the time its limit resets, and the census used to wait a flat 61 seconds, so a long reset used up its three tries and failed the run. It waits until the reset that Retry-After (seconds or a date), RateLimit-Reset or X-RateLimit-Reset names, plus a second, capped at 15 minutes by `-MaxRateLimitWaitSeconds`. An answer that names no reset still waits `-RateLimitWaitSeconds`, and a fourth limit in a row still fails the source. The run log also says whether GitLab was read with a token, since a token raises the limit.
- The source census reads the Morphe Patch Tracker again. Its list now carries a couple of bundles twice under keys that differ only in case (immortalzeus:dev and ImmortalZeus:dev), and the census refused the whole file as unreadable JSON. It reads those keys as they are now and counts each repository once, in PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 alike.
- The final APK check now holds Hide suggested users on profiles to its own contract. It finds both places from the clean DEX alone: the profile screen's suggested accounts carousel, which has to hand its list to the extension right before Threads' own null check and cast the answer back, and the header row, which has to ask first thing on its path and leave by its check's other side through a local nothing reads. A build without the patch has to leave both as Threads wrote them, with no call to the extension anywhere.
- The final APK check now holds Copy text on long press to its own contract whenever Settings is selected. Every override check in the post row has to carry the patch's hook, which hands the override and its own action to the extension in a free local and casts the answer back, and PostText has to ask about its selection switch first thing. A build without Settings has to leave both exactly as Threads wrote them.
- The build classpath inventory now records a SHA-256 of settings.gradle.kts, patches/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and gradle/verification-metadata.xml, and the release receipt refuses an inventory whose hash for any of them differs from the checkout, naming the file. Before, only the settings script was checked, so a changed plugin version or dependency pin could leave an old inventory standing for the new build. Each hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's raw bytes.
- The source census reads Jman's Patch Bundle Registry now, through its registration file and the paged Threads list, because the old bundle files there answer 404. It follows the list's own total across short pages within a request and row budget, reads renamed repositories under their current names, and counts a repository as a Threads bundle only for a current release with verified metadata. History, unverified entries and a bare registration are reported but not promoted, and a list it can't finish reading fails the census. The source ledger points its Jman entry at the registry too, with HushThreads' registration there as the listing's evidence.
- Updated the build wrapper to Gradle 9.8.1, which fixes three high security advisories. The build advisory check now checks the recorded Gradle distribution separately from component libraries and refuses missing or unreadable version evidence, including when online component checks are skipped.
- A fixture test checks on 451 that both of the post row's long press override checks and PostText's selection flag go through the extension, and that a jump straight to an override check or a selection flag written over before PostText copies it stops the patch.
- The release receipt now asks OSV about the plugin classpath that builds and signs the bundle too, from an inventory settings.gradle.kts writes after each bundle build, and reports it apart from what the bundle carries, with its own exception list. A version that was only asked for and resolved to another is listed as a request, and a missing inventory or a dependency that didn't resolve stops the release instead of reading as clean.
- The bundle build holds the Android Gradle plugin's jose4j at 0.9.6 and jdom2 at 2.0.6.1, the patch releases that fix their high advisories, so the plugin classpath has none left.

HushTelegram v0.0.23 has 67 patches for the Google Play build of Telegram 13.1.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72371) and telegram.org's Telegram 13.1.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72299). It's on Morphe patcher 2.1.0 like 0.0.22, so Morphe Manager 2.3.0 or newer still loads it. Nearly all of it came from your reports again, and it changes something for #9, #29, #39, #41, #45, #48, #49 and #50. Calls can be recorded to a file on your phone, and a record button on the call screen does it for just the call you're on. View-once and timed photos and videos can stay in the chat after you open them, or get copied to Download/Telegram. Ghost mode can hide typing and your online status now. With UnifiedPush, reaction notifications can play a sound and name custom emoji, and turning UnifiedPush on also switches on Telegram's own background connection so messages arrive while the app is closed. New in this release

- `Ghost mode` has two more parts, `Hide typing` and `Hide online status`, both off by default. With Ghost mode and `Hide typing` on, people in a chat don't see that you're typing, recording a voice message or sending a file, in secret chats too. With `Hide online status` on, Telegram isn't told that you're online while you use it. Going offline still goes out, so your account shows as offline when you leave. The diagnostic report counts what each one kept back. (#45)

- `UnifiedPush notifications` has a new switch, `Sound for reaction notifications`, off by default. Telegram keeps every reaction notification silent. Turn it on and they play the sound and vibration you picked in Telegram's Notifications and Sounds > Reactions. (#41)

- Reaction notifications with `UnifiedPush notifications` now cover custom emoji reactions too. Once Telegram has loaded that emoji on your phone, the notification names the regular emoji it stands for. (#41)

- `Disable call debug upload` has a new switch, `Record calls`, off by default. Turn it on and every call is saved on your phone as one .m4a file with both sides in it, named for when the call began, in Recordings/Telegram calls (Music/Telegram calls on Android 11 and older). Voice chats and live streams you're in get saved the same way. The other person isn't told. On Android 9 it needs Telegram's storage permission. (#39)

- `Record button on calls`, off by default, puts a round record button on the call screen right under the minimize arrow. Tap it to record just the call you're on. With `Record calls` on, the button starts out red and a tap skips recording that one call, keeping what was already recorded. It hides along with the rest of the call screen's buttons, and the choice ends with the call. (#39)

- A new `Ways in` section on the HushTelegram settings page has a switch for each way to open them, all on by default. They are the HushTelegram row on Telegram's Settings page, a long press on the Telegram title in the chat list, the row in the side menu, and the shortcut in the menu you get from holding Telegram's icon. A way you turn off acts like stock Telegram. The row, the long press and the side menu entry are gone, and the shortcut is taken off the launcher, pinned copies included. One way always stays on so you can get back in, and turning off the last one puts the switch back with a short message. No restart needed. `Lock HushTelegram settings` holds these switches like the rest. (#29)

- `Save downloaded files` has a third switch, `Also save view-once and timed media`, off by default. With it on, view-once and self-destructing photos, videos, voice messages and video messages get copied to Download/Telegram once they download, readable like any other file. Secret chats stay in Telegram whatever the switches say. From a chat that doesn't allow saving, `Also save from chats that don't allow saving` has to be on as well. (#9)

- `Keep deleted messages` has a new switch, `Keep view-once and timed media`, off by default. Turn it on and a view-once or self-destructing photo, video, voice message or video message someone sends you stays in the chat after you open it. There's no countdown, and you can open it again as often as you like. Secret chats work as usual. Timed media you send stays on your phone too. (#9)

Fixes

- With `Hide reactions under messages` on, TalkBack no longer reads out reactions you can't see. A message reads the same as one nobody reacted to, and Saved Messages tags are still read since they still show. (#48)

- Leaving `Message times with seconds` out in Morphe Manager now really leaves it out. `Keep deleted messages` used to pull the whole patch back in, so its switch still showed in the Hush settings. Now it takes along only the part it needs to mark a message deleted. (#49)

- With `UnifiedPush` on, Hush now also turns on Telegram's own `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` once your push app hands over its address, so messages come in while Telegram is closed instead of when you next open it. It only does that if you never set either switch yourself, and the notification report says what turned them on. (#50)

- The whole-app walk gets past Android asking for contacts or photos over the screen it's opening. It says no (Don't allow, or Not now on Telegram's own contacts prompt, never Allow or Continue) and opens the screen again. If the ask keeps coming back, the walk's problem line names it instead of a bare "would not open".

- The release build stage writes down how long the full gate took, the same way preflight already does, so a slow gate shows up next to the earlier timing.

How to update

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.3.0 or newer. That's the same floor as 0.0.22, so if you patched that one you're set.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get the right Telegram. From Google Play that's 13.1.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72371), which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) and Uptodown also carry. From telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android) it's 13.1.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72299). The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from 0.0.22? Patch the APK of the same build you're on and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. Your settings and chats stay. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put a patched app over one signed with a different key. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, that's Telegram refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build, the Play one included. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. On phones where Firebase notifications don't come through, try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy. It turns those two on for you unless you've set them yourself.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The new Ways in section on that page decides which of those (plus the side menu row and the icon shortcut) stay.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

Forwarding, screenshots and the rest of the restriction stay as they are. (#43)

- `Disable double-tap reactions` has two new switches under it, both off by default. `Hide reactions under messages` stops the row of reactions from being drawn under each message, and `Hide the reaction picker` removes the row of reactions at the top of the long-press menu along with the panel it opens. Nothing stored is changed, so turning a switch off brings everything back. Tags in Saved Messages still show. (#48)

- `Hide recommendations` has a new switch under it, `Hide trending packs`, off by default. - `Hide Premium, gifts and Stars` has a new switch under it, `Hide emoji statuses`, off by default. Turn it on and the emoji a Premium account puts next to its name is gone from chats, the chat list and profiles, so you see the plain Premium star instead. Your own status hides on your phone too, but everyone else still sees it. Picking a new status for a channel you run still saves.

- `Hide Premium, gifts and Stars` also has `Unlock Premium app icons`, off by default. With it on, Premium, Turbo and Nox in Telegram's App Icon list (Settings, Appearance) have no lock and switch your home screen icon like the others, instead of opening the Premium sheet. They show in the list even where Telegram sells no Premium. Only the icon on your phone changes. (#13, #14)

- `Hide Premium, gifts and Stars` also has `Emoji status on this phone`, off by default. With it on, the star next to Telegram at the top of the chat list opens the emoji status picker without Premium, and the emoji you pick, animated ones too, shows there on your phone. Nobody else sees it and nothing goes to Telegram. Picking no status puts the star back. (#14)

- `Hide channel bar buttons` has a new switch under it, `Hide channel share button`, off by default. With it on, the round share button beside channel posts goes away, in the channel itself and in any chat a channel post gets forwarded to. A post's own menu still forwards it. Bots, people's media in public groups and Saved Messages keep their button.

- `Stop usage reports` has a new switch under it, `Ghost mode`, off by default. It has two parts, `No read receipts` and `View stories anonymously`, which start on. With Ghost mode on, people don't see the messages you read as read, in private chats, groups and secret chats, and voice messages you play stay unplayed for them. Stories you watch don't add you to the viewer list. Sending a message in a chat still marks it read, since Telegram does that on its side, and your other devices keep showing chats you read here as unread. The diagnostic report counts the read receipts and story views it kept back. (#45)

- `Hide popular apps` has a new switch under it, `Block new channels and groups`, off by default. It's meant as a parental control. With it on, joining a channel or group doesn't go through, whether it's from search, an invite link or a shared folder link, and a channel or group you aren't in won't open, forums included. A short message says new chats are blocked in the HushTelegram settings. Chats you're already in work as before. Turn on `Lock HushTelegram settings` too, or the switch can just be turned off again. While Telegram is connected, someone reacting to one of your messages gets the same "reacted to your message" notification Telegram shows from a push, once per reaction. Telegram's own `Reactions` switch in Notifications and Sounds still has to be on. (#41)

Fixes

- With `Full screen videos turn either way` or `Turn videos only from the full screen button` on, turning your phone upright no longer takes a video out of full screen. Telegram ends full screen on its own once the phone has been on its side and comes back upright, which with either switch on left the video standing up and stuck that way until you tapped the button again. Full screen now lasts until you tap the button or close the video. (#27)

- When a settings editor can't save what you typed, the reason under the field stays on screen at large text sizes with the keyboard up. The cursor used to scroll it right back out of sight.

- The API key field in `Translation service` uses the same letters as the fields above it. Its hint used to show in a typewriter font.

- On a narrow screen or with large text, the HushTelegram settings search box says Search instead of a cut-off "Search settings". TalkBack still reads it as Search settings.

- `Save downloaded files` no longer puts the wrong file in Download/Telegram when two documents have the same name and size. Telegram stores a document under its own name, and when a second one of that name and size arrives it opens the first one's file without downloading anything. That file used to be copied as the second document. Now it stays in Telegram.

- With the HushTelegram settings open, tapping a Telegram link in another app now closes them and shows the chat. The chat used to open behind the settings, so you had to back out of them to see it. Tapping Telegram's icon still brings the settings back as you left them.

- With TalkBack on, tapping `Pause` at the top of the HushTelegram settings now moves focus to the card that says Telegram will pause, where its Undo button is. Before, focus went nowhere once the button stepped aside.

- In the HushTelegram settings, the search box's outline now goes all the way around while you type. The X that clears the search used to cover its right end.

- With `Keep Telegram's files in internal storage` on, files Telegram downloaded before you turned it on open from Android/data again instead of downloading a second copy. New downloads still land in Internal storage/Telegram. (#7)

- Chats hidden with `Hide picked chats` no longer count toward the unread numbers on the folder tabs, and hiding or unhiding one updates them right away, on every account you're signed in to. The app badge still counts their unread messages, since they keep their notifications. (#24)

- The settings lock now covers `Emoji next to the chat list title` too. While the settings are locked, tapping it shows the lock note instead of opening the editor. (#17)

- Turning `Hide folder tab counters` on or off changes the folder tabs right away. Before, the counts stayed as they were until Telegram restarted.

- `Open a folder at launch` brings the folder you picked into view. With more folders than fit across the screen, a pick past the edge used to open selected but out of sight until you scrolled the tabs. With fewer folders the tabs look just as they did.

- TalkBack reads a settings section's state once. Section titles like Ads and Look and feel said "Collapsed, Collapsed" (or "Expanded, Expanded") before the name, because TalkBack already says the state for anything that opens and closes. They still read as headings. (#18)

- Long words in the HushTelegram settings break where their language hyphenates them. At large text sizes German compounds used to split at whatever letter filled the line, and a name like Firebase-Push-Registrierung moved its hyphen to the start of the next line. Dialog titles, dialog messages and choice lists break the same way now.

- `UnifiedPush notifications` makes one set of encryption keys the first time it signs up, even when Telegram's own sign-up and a new address from the push app ask for them at the same moment. Two sets could get made, with Telegram signed up on the one that wasn't kept, so turning the switch off later didn't hand notifications back to Firebase until Telegram restarted. Keys that couldn't be saved also stay out of later sign-ups until the next start.

- `Keep edit history` starts a message's history over when what it kept for that message can't be read anymore. Before, one damaged entry meant that message never kept an earlier text again.

- Patching with `Use registered Telegram API credentials` from the Morphe command line explains a missing API ID. The command line drops a bare number like `-O apiId=12345` before the patch sees it, and the old message only asked you to fill in both fields. Quote the ID as `-O "apiId='12345'"` and it goes through.

- With `Hide channel Mute button` on, the bar at the bottom of a channel comes back the way Telegram last set it once the channel stops showing Mute. If Telegram hid the bar while it was held back, or changed it with the switch off, the bar used to reappear anyway.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** A release walk now has to be a walk of the APK it says it walked. `scripts/walk-app.ps1` leaves `patch-artifact.json` next to the signed APK (its SHA-256 and signing certificate, package and version, the fixture and bundle it came from, the patches picked) and the receipt carries it. Publish turns the walk down when the installed APK's hash doesn't match that record, the APK came from another bundle or fixture or left a patch out, or the package or version is wrong. It also refuses a walk with recorded problems, times that can't be right, or a scenario from `scripts/walk-scenarios.json` that never opened, so a shortened `-SettingsPages` list can't pass as a full walk. A signed-out walk is reported as a settings smoke and a signed-in one as feature acceptance. `-SkipPatch` walks the same APK again by its record.
* **Tooling:** The patch checks (`verify-all-patches.ps1`, `verify-patch-selections.ps1`, the release receipt and `patch-for-device.ps1`) now run the CLI with `--validate`, so a fingerprint that matches more than one method fails instead of patching the first one it finds. A run kept with `-KeepIn` from before this change gets patched again.
* **Tooling:** The patch selection check (`verify-patch-selections.ps1`) no longer fails its broken options file case on morphe-desktop 1.19.1. That version prints its stack lines in italics, and the style codes hid the lines the check reads.
* **Tooling:** The source census reads Jman's Patch Bundle Registry through its catalog API now. The registry dropped the snapshot the audit used to read, so that check answered 404. Preflight also checks that the census is from the last 14 days. Before, only the index stage did, and by then the release was already public.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.2.0 or newer. Older Managers can't load this release, so update Manager first.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get the right Telegram. From Google Play that's 13.1.1 (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72371), which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) and Uptodown also carry. From telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android) it's 13.1.0 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72299). The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from an earlier HushTelegram? Patch the APK of the same build you're on and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. If you're on the Play build, that means 13.1.1 now, since Play's 13.1.0 isn't supported anymore. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put a patched app over one signed with a different key. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, that's Telegram refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build, the Play one included. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. Phones where Firebase notifications don't come through can also try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The side menu is the `Side menu` switch on the Chat list page.

## Validation

All 1504 runtime tests passed locally, and all 518 patch tests passed too, along with both Android lints (the shared library and the Telegram extension). Every one of the 67 patches applied without forcing to telegram.org's Telegram 13.1.0 (version code 72299) and to the Google Play build of 13.1.1 (version code 72371). For each patched build the release receipt checked the package name, version, manifest, native libraries and zip alignment.

telegram.org's build, patched from this exact bundle, was installed over an older HushTelegram on an Android 13 emulator without clearing its data. Then the whole HushTelegram settings screen was walked, 16 screens in all, with no crash. That emulator isn't signed in to Telegram, so the walk ended at Telegram's sign-in screen. Android's own code check on the same emulator found nothing to complain about in the patched app, the same result as stock Telegram.

Morphe Manager 2.2.0 was checked too, on an Android 14 emulator. It loaded this bundle from a file, patched telegram.org's 13.1.0 with `Black and white launch logo` picked in Expert mode, installed it over an older HushTelegram and the app opened fine.

HushGram moves to Instagram 453.0.0.57.79 and Morphe patcher 2.1.0, so you'll need Morphe Manager 2.3.0 or newer. Behind the scenes

- When patching for a phone stops on an Instagram build with no reviewed coverage, the message now names the builds that have it, so you know which one to patch.

- Patching for a phone without `-Apk` takes the declared Instagram build from the fixture folder the way the release gate does, `.apks` bundles included. It used to skip `.apks` and take any file with the version in its name.

- The whole-app walk takes one more look, after a short pause, at a settings heading it caught mid-animation. It used to call the heading missing and fail the walk when a section was still opening or folding.

- When a settings heading isn't there, the whole-app walk says so as soon as the list stops moving. It used to keep swiping up past the top of the list, 24 times each way.

- Patch results, records and the patch catalog are read as strict JSON. A file that names a field twice could read as a pass and a failure at once, so it's refused.

- The release notes check refuses a bullet scoped to a patch name in any section after 0.0.17, Unreleased included, so each bullet names its patch in the text. It used to pass any dated section.

- The native runner reads the user limit the way Android 17 prints it, "Maximum supported switchable users", so it runs on an API 37 emulator. It used to stop there, saying the device takes one user.

- The release check reads an index description naming only the Instagram build as the published release's facts, still under that version's heading. A retarget held at the published version used to fail every push.

- The release check holds a published receipt to the coverage census its own commit reviewed. Once a retarget replaced the old build's entry, the shipped receipt read as uncertified and the check failed on every push.

- The source audit reports a source it couldn't read past a rate limit as unread, and fails GitLab code search when a limit keeps a hit's project unread. Both used to be treated as gone.

- The source audit waits out a rate limit for as long as the forge's Retry-After asks, up to five minutes. A longer one, like GitLab's hourly limit, fails that source at once and says when it resets.

- The source audit leaves a source unread when a rate limit stops a branch comparison, instead of reporting the branch as new work. A server error on a GitLab hit's project now fails the search too.

- Updated to Morphe patcher 2.1.0, so patching needs Morphe Manager 2.3.0 or newer. On a computer, use morphe-desktop 1.20.0 or newer. The dependency audit now reviews Morphe Desktop 1.20.0.

- The native runner has a share case for the share sheet stand-in. The share and its sender always come through. Instagram's links are the only ones cleaned, and just while `Sanitize sharing links` is on.

- Morphe Manager now knows the armeabi-v7a, x86 and x86_64 builds of Instagram too, so an older 32-bit phone is pointed at the build it can install instead of the arm64 one. Reported in #346.

- `Tap to play` keeps a Reels auto-scroll allowance for the next Reel. Feed and unidentified players can't spend it, and a real tap on Feed still works.

- `Group Instagram's notifications` keeps summaries while their notifications remain. Turning grouping off or removing one notification no longer dismisses the others. Pending posts stay protected while Android catches up. One notification uses the singular count label.

- Turning off profile posts as a list, or pausing HushGram, cancels an automatic opening that was still waiting for the grid.

- Canceling a download can finish while DNS, proxy discovery or response setup is still waiting. Late responses can't write a file, and repeated cancellations keep a bounded number of workers.

- The downloader closes opened response streams on success and failure. Cache bytes stay only after a successful close.

- Closing `Save profile picture` stops its fetch even when the general background workers are busy.

- `Download any video` adds source metadata to JPEG photos saved through Save all and Choose pages, as it does for a single photo. Videos and other image formats stay unchanged.

- Download history repairs a partially written record before its next write. Later saves remain listed after a restart.

- A failed PIN save keeps the setup form open and reports the failure. The PIN and its retry counters are saved together.

- PIN retry limits still apply in the current process when their counters can't be saved.

- `HushGram settings` saves a timed lock and its wait together. Lock, unlock and wait actions no longer report success after a failed write.

- `HushGram settings` checks the current lock before an editor or delayed action saves. Imports and Undo check again at their write boundary, and a held Undo remains available until its original deadline.

- Font imports finish reading and closing their provider before replacing a live font. Failed or stale imports leave the current files alone, and reopening settings can't start a competing copy.

- Replacing an imported app font keeps Restart now available even when the font choice hasn't changed.

- Settings backups restore large selections of hidden Instagram settings rows. Selecting all 161 supported rows no longer causes that choice to be skipped.

- `Hide suggested posts` keeps native paging when a filtered page retains a real post, even before its list is displayed. Header-only pages can still finish.

- `Glass tab bar` blur recovers after a temporary capture failure on a still screen. Automatic retries stay bounded, and pending work stops when the bar leaves or HushGram pauses.

- `Story text fonts` puts local fonts before Instagram's paid section, so selecting one doesn't open a Plus offer. Instagram's paid fonts keep their subscription checks. Reported in #275 and #325.

- `View stories anonymously` keeps your own story, Create and special tray entries in their original positions during watched-story sorting. Ordinary story rings keep their order within the unseen and watched groups.

- `HushGram settings` requires Android 9 on every ABI, including the two 32-bit APKs Instagram ships for Android 8. Manifest checks verify that floor and preserve any higher vendor minimum.

- `Show if a profile follows you` waits for unique followers to match the account's count before recording recent unfollowers. Short lists and older queued saves can't replace a newer snapshot, and failed saves can be retried.

- `HushGram settings` lets go of a closed screen or dialog. The moving title used to keep every one you'd opened in memory until Instagram restarted.

- `Convert to keep the full size` asks the phone's encoder for limited range BT.709 color. Left to choose, some encoders write a file other apps show with shifted colors.

Other changes

New in this release

Fixes

HushPinterest 0.0.13 has 33 patches for Pinterest 14.41.0. It's the first one built on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer before you patch. Older Manager builds can't open this bundle.

The new patch is GmsCore support, for phones that run microG-RE instead of Google Play services. It sends Pinterest's Google sign-in and push notifications through microG-RE. It isn't picked by default, so if you don't use microG-RE nothing changes for you.

Patch 14.41.0 with the same signing key you used before and install it over your current HushPinterest. Your settings stay as they are.

## What's new

- New GmsCore support patch, for phones that run microG-RE instead of Google Play services. Pinterest's Google sign-in and push notifications go through microG-RE, so Continue with Google opens microG-RE's sign-in. Before, it asked Play services and the account got turned down. It's left out of the default selection since without microG-RE those requests have nowhere to go. Pick it in Expert mode and Spoof signature for Google sign-in comes along with it. (#15)
- The patches are now built on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so you'll need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer to apply them. Older Manager builds can't load the bundle.

## Behind the scenes

- A release can't go public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk` and stops before GitHub or the index if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Pinterest crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle.
- A device lease another session happens to be reading no longer stops a run partway. The check waits a moment and tries again, and a lease that stays locked still stops it.
- New `scripts/walk-app.ps1` patches Pinterest from the release bundle and installs it on a leased phone or emulator. Then it opens the home feed, the patched screens and every Hush settings page, and writes the receipt publish asks for. Only a full walk with no Pinterest crash earns a PASS.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.0.0 or newer.
2. Add HushPinterest as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushPinterest
3. Download Pinterest 14.41.0, version code `14418010`. APKMirror has it as an arm64-v8a bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer. Pick that file in Manager and it merges the parts before patching.
4. Uninstall the stock Pinterest first, since Android won't put one over the other. Save anything you keep only on the phone before you do. Your boards and pins come back when you sign in.
5. Sign in with your email and a Pinterest password. If you joined through Google or Facebook, tap `Forgot your password?` on Pinterest's login page to set one first. On a phone with microG-RE, pick GmsCore support when you patch and Continue with Google goes to microG-RE's sign-in instead.
6. Right after your first patch, export Morphe Manager's signing key (Settings, then System, then Import & export, then Signing key) and keep it somewhere private. Updates only install over a Pinterest signed with that same key.

Already on HushPinterest? Update Manager, then skip steps 4 and 5. Patch 14.41.0 with the same key and install it over the one you have.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Pinterest APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#install). `SHA256SUMS.txt` is signed with the HushPinterest release key, fingerprint `FCE5 ECE3 182A 647B 3AF2  C5ED 2DC3 5E8D 5C00 E8A6`. [How to check a download](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest#verify-a-release-download).

## Reported issues

- #15: GmsCore support is new in this release, for signing in with Google on a phone that has microG-RE instead of Play services.

## Validation

All 241 patch tests and 1069 extension tests passed on this commit, none skipped. The bundle attached here was patched onto a real Pinterest 14.41.0 bundle from APKMirror with Morphe's desktop patcher, and all 33 patches applied without forcing. `release-receipt-0.0.13.json` records that result, the bundle's hash and what patching changed in the app's manifest.

Before release, this exact bundle patched a Pinterest that went on an Android emulator for a walk through the whole app: the home feed, a pin, notifications, searches for pins, boards and people, and all ten HushPinterest settings pages. Pinterest didn't crash once.

GmsCore support was tried on an emulator with microG-RE installed. Pinterest opened microG-RE's Google sign-in at launch, and Continue with Google went on to microG-RE's account screen. That emulator had no Google account added, so a full sign-in wasn't done there.

HushPinterest 0.0.12 has 32 patches for Pinterest 14.41.0. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. This one moves to Pinterest's newest version and adds a lot of new switches, every one of them off until you turn it on. Filter feed can hide video pins and pins with words you mute. Keep Home feed stops Home from reloading on its own when you come back to it, and Show posted date puts the day a pin went up under its title. Download pins can copy or share the picture itself now, and its rows show in the full-screen pin menu too. Downloads also stopped settling for the smaller copy now and then.

It's a new Pinterest version. So far APKMirror only has 14.41.0 as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching. Patch it with the same signing key you used before and install it over your current HushPinterest, and your settings stay as they are. On a phone older than Android 12L, keep 0.0.11 and Pinterest 14.40.0 for now.

## What's new

- The patches now target Pinterest 14.41.0, the newest stable release. 14.40.0 is no longer supported. So far APKMirror has 14.41.0 only as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching.
- Download pin now shows in the full-screen pin menu some accounts get from the three dots on a pin, along with the other Hush rows, and Pinterest's own Download row in that menu gives way to it. Before, only the smaller pop-up menu had them.
- Download pins has a new switch, Copy image, that starts off. It adds a Copy image row under Download pin, in the small pin menu and in the full-screen one, and puts the full-size picture on the clipboard so you can paste it into a chat or a notes app. Video pins don't get the row. If the picture is too big, isn't really an image, or takes too long, you're told so and your clipboard stays as it was. (#11)
- Download pins also has Share image, another switch that starts off. Its row sits under Copy image and opens Android's share menu with the full-size picture itself rather than a link, so the app you pick gets the image. Video pins don't get it, and if the picture can't be fetched you get a short note instead of the share menu. (#11)
- Long-press download has three new switches on the Pin actions page: Hide Save, Hide Send and Hide Search image in the long-press menu. Each takes that one Pinterest button out of the round menu you get by holding a pin in a grid, and the pin itself still saves, shares and searches as before. They work with Download off too. If everything would be hidden and Download is off, the menu stays Pinterest's own rather than opening empty. All three start off. (#11)
- Black comments now covers the strip under the status bar too. On 14.41.0 the comments fill the whole screen, and that strip stayed dark gray above the black list on photo and video pins alike.
- Downloads no longer save the smaller copy now and then when the original is there. Finding the original asks Pinterest's media server a few quick questions, and one asked just as both lookup helpers were wrapping up the last was turned away, so the download settled for the size the feed showed. It now waits a moment for a helper to come free.
- Copy media link no longer overwrites something you copied after it. When a pin shows only a smaller size, the link to that size goes on the clipboard right away, and it becomes the original's link once Pinterest's media server answers, but only if the clipboard still holds that copy. Before, nothing was copied until the answer came, and a slow answer could replace whatever you'd copied in the meantime.
- Save list no longer hangs when the app holding the picked file stops answering. Each save gets 30 seconds in all, then you're told to check the file, and a late answer from that app doesn't add another message or remove anything. While that app is still busy, a new list says to try later instead of opening a picker. Everything that talks to the file's app now runs on its own helper, never on the screen's thread, including the clean-up after a list that couldn't be written while HushPinterest was paused.
- A list that isn't written no longer deletes an empty file you picked to write over. Only an empty file made since the picker opened gets removed. Any other file is left where it is, and you're told so.
- Save list leaves out a source link that hides a session code behind an encoded `;` (`%3B`, that encoded again, or a longer spelling some servers still read as `;`), the way it already left out a plain `;jsessionid=`. The pin's ID, title and Pinterest link still go in. Ordinary encoded spaces and accented letters stay exactly as given.
- Queue selected and Queue pins stay off until something chosen can actually be saved. A pin with no picture address, or a video Pinterest only streams, doesn't turn them on anymore, though Save list still takes those pins. A mix still queues what it can and counts the rest as unsupported.
- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Pinterest was patched with, not just a short summary. For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of this changelog, and the description was one paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's changes after the summary, starting with this one.
- Hide comments has a second switch, Hide suggested replies, for the row of ready-made replies like "Yum!" and "Came out great!" next to the comment box. You can still write your own comment. It starts off, and the two switches don't turn each other on. (#14)
- Hide AI-labeled pins has a second switch, Hide pins that say they're AI, for AI pins Pinterest doesn't label. It takes a pin whose title or description says something like "AI art", "AI generated", #aiart, "made with AI", Midjourney, Stable Diffusion or PixAI, and pins from sites that only host AI images, like pixai.art and Civitai. It goes by the pin's own words, so a pin that just says "AI" stays, and names like Ai Weiwei or the Portuguese "aí" are left alone. Boards named that way stay too. It starts off, and diagnostics count these pins apart from the labeled ones.
- Hide closeup buttons has a third switch, Hide Search image label on pins. Pinterest puts a "Search image" label on the lens button for your first two pins each day, and with this on the lens shows without it, the way it looks from the third pin on. Tapping the lens still searches. It starts off and sits under Hide lens button on the Interface page. (#13)
- New Filter feed patch, with a Hide video pins switch on the Feed page. It takes pins that play a video out of your home feed, search, related pins and boards, idea pins with video included. Photos and GIFs stay. It starts off.
- Filter feed also has Muted words, a row on the Feed page where you type words and phrases you don't want to see. A pin whose title or description has one of them leaves the same lists. Capitals don't matter and only whole words count, so "cake" takes out "Wedding Cake Ideas" but not cupcakes. The list holds 50 entries of up to 40 characters, starts empty, and goes into settings files with your switches. Boards named after a muted word stay.
- New Keep Home feed patch, with its switch on the Feed page. Pinterest reloads Home with new pins on its own when you come back after five minutes or more, when you pick the Home tab again after a while and when you back out of a search, and the pin you were about to open is gone. With this on, Home stays where you left it. Pull down whenever you want new pins. The new pins prompt, a second tap on the Home tab and a pin you open from a notification still load as before. It starts off.
- New Show posted date patch, with its switch on the Interface page. Pinterest sends the day each pin was posted but never shows it, and with this on you see "Posted" and that day under the title when you open a pin. A pin without a date just doesn't get the line. The date follows the language HushPinterest shows and your phone's time zone. It starts off and shows from the next pin you open. (#11)
- With Debug logging on, the line for a kept pin also says whether Pinterest marked it as a repin or as saved to one of your boards. It shows only that the field is set, never which board.
- The Feed page has a new row under the AI switches, Pinterest's own AI setting. It opens the page where Pinterest lets you see fewer AI pins among the ones it picks for you, since neither that page nor the switches catch every AI pin alone. It's there whenever Hide AI-labeled pins is patched in.

## Behind the scenes

- The pin model fixture test also checks the fields Hide video pins reads, the two inside Pinterest's video and idea pin models included, and the grid title that the AI words and video filters use to tell a pin from other models.
- The pre-push and release checks take a declared build kept as APKMirror's `.apkm` bundle, since that's the only way 14.41.0 ships. The bug report form's example names a bundle too, and the release step keeps whatever kind of file the form names.
- The release gate's advisory check works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 again. Since 0.0.11, any failed OSV request stopped it there with an "Unable to find type" error. A dropped connection or a busy server now gets asked again in 5.1, the way it already did in PowerShell 7.
- The README's Help now goes through why Android might refuse the install. It says where Manager keeps its signing key, so an update that won't go over your patched copy can be fixed without losing your settings. It also covers stock Pinterest and the unknown apps prompt.
- The README sends people on v0.0.11 to Pinterest 14.40.0 again, the build that release patches, and names 14.41.0 as the next release's build. It had pointed them at 14.41.0, which v0.0.11 refuses. The release's prepare step now stops while the README still names a next release, so it gets rewritten for the new build before a release is cut.
- The patch verifier checks how the long-press hide switches tell Pinterest's buttons apart. The sorter has to read the held button's own id and send Save, Send and both search ids to the right answer, with the ids found the way the patch finds them, and a build without them has to keep the plain answer.
- The bug report form lists Filter feed among the patches you can tick. It was the one patch the form left out, and the release check stopped on that.
- The release check and the publish step leave a GitHub description alone when it names no version, patch count or Pinterest build, since there's nothing in it to go stale. One that names any of them still has to match the release. This release would have stopped on the shorter description the repository uses now.
- The source census reads Jman's bundle registry again. On October 14 the registry took down the files the audit read and now serves the same list from its own site, so every audit since stopped on a missing file. It reads all of the site's pages, not only the first hundred releases.
- The device scripts write their lease times in UTC with a `Z` at the end. They used `+00:00`, and the other tools sharing the test phone took a lease written that way as already expired. They also read a `Z` time as UTC now. Before, a busy phone's expiry was read as local clock time, so an expired lease looked hours from ending.
- The script tests now clean up after themselves. The pre-push cases remove the worktree the hook builds in, and a passing host reference run deletes its report folder. Each run used to leave both in the temp directory.

PixelBoard v18.5.3-V1 updates the base Google Keyboard to the official **Gboard v18.5.3 Release**, introduces a built-in **in-app update checker** positioned conveniently right on the main Gboard settings screen.

## Summary
PixelBoard v1.2.0 introduces Features Menu accessibility and TalkBack focus fixes, fused APK native split readiness verification for voice typing, automated clipboard screenshot observer synchronization, Sign-to-Text (ASL translation) camera integration, smart auto-correction with primary-key revert, and refined typing suggestions on top of Google's latest **Gboard v18.4.1 Release** (`18.4.1.985164140-release-arm64-v8a`).

---

## What's New in This Release (v18.4.1-V7 / Patch v1.2.0)

### 1. Features Menu Accessibility & TalkBack Navigation ([#48](https://github.com/Akshayykadam/PixelBoard/issues/48))
- **Screen Reader Announcements**: Resolved an issue where opening the features menu / "More options" (`AccessPointsPanel`, `AccessPointsPanelV2`, `AccessPointsPanelViewPage`) failed to notify TalkBack and accessibility services of window state changes.
- **Automated Focus Traversal**: Sets accessibility pane title (`resolvePaneTitle`), dispatches `AccessibilityEvent.TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED`, and automatically shifts focus to the first accessible tool or keycap (`SoftKeyView` / button).

### 2. Dictation JNI Readiness for Fused APKs & Offline Voice Typing ([#50](https://github.com/Akshayykadam/PixelBoard/issues/50))
- **Fused Base APK Compatibility**: Direct JNI library loading verification (`NativeLibHelper.c("dictation_jni", false)`) prevents dictation readiness checks from failing on fused APKs that lack Play feature-split markers.
- **Fused Target Hooks**: Added seamless bytecode patching for fused readiness target `slc` (`Lqeq;->e(Lqem;)Z`).
- **Offline Language Pack Download Interception**: Resolved offline voice typing download failures (such as traditional Chinese `zh-TW`) by handling offline recognition pack URL resolution cleanly.

### 3. Clipboard & Screenshot Observer Synchronization ([#52](https://github.com/Akshayykadam/PixelBoard/issues/52))
- **Foreground Screenshot Observer**: Added `ensureScreenshotObserver(handler)` calling `ClipboardDataHandler.q(true)` on `onStartInputView`, ensuring screenshot chips and clipboard items update immediately on display.
- **XML Default Overrides**: Enforced `defaultValue = "true"` directly in `res/xml/setting_clipboard.xml` for `enable_screenshot_in_clipboard` and `pref_key_enable_clipboard`.
- **Emoji Suggestions**: Unconditionally enables `pref_key_enable_emoji_suggestion` as default `true`.

### 4. Sign-to-Text (Signboard ASL Real-Time Translation)
- **American Sign Language Camera Translation**: Enabled native camera gesture translation to convert American Sign Language into text on supported devices.
- **Phenotype Flag Enforcement**: Activated `enable_signboard`, `signboard_prompt_manual_trigger`, `on_demand_feature_split`, `auto_show_signboard`, `signboard_auto_show_prompt`, `signboard_download`, `signboard_download_dialog`, `signboard_move_ap_prompt`, and `use_4c_in_signboard`.

### 5. Smart Auto-Correction & Typing Refinements ([#52](https://github.com/Akshayykadam/PixelBoard/issues/52))
- **Primary-Key Revert**: Enforced `auto_correct_with_replace_text = true` and `enable_revert_auto_correct_on_pk = true` (enables reverting auto-corrections via backspace/tap on physical and soft keyboards).
- **Out-of-the-Box Auto-Correction**: Pre-seeds `pref_key_auto_correction = true` by default.
- **Typo Protection**: Tuned `intended_oov_min_count` from `1L` to `2L` so mistyped words typed once (e.g. "olle") are not mistakenly learned into user vocabulary, allowing spacebar auto-correction to properly commit corrections.

### 6. Version 1.2.0 Synchronization
- **System-Wide Alignment**: Synchronized patch bundle version `1.2.0` across Gradle build properties, settings UI, preferences metadata, and bundle manifests.

- **GmsCore support is now ON by default** - Google Sign-In works against MicroG RE with no extra toggles. Requires MicroG RE (`app.revanced.android.gms`) with a Google account added in it.
- Automatically pulls in **Spoof signature** (original Play certificate) for Firebase / API-key checks.

## HDO Box (new)
- **Remove ads** - neutralises the Unity Ads plugin.
- **Disable analytics** - disables Firebase Analytics collection and blocks re-enabling it.

### 対応バージョン

- 追加：YouTube 21.30.216（Morphe 公式のパッチの安定版の対象）、YouTube 21.44.528（ストアの最新版）、
  Reddit 2026.40.0（公式のパッチの安定版の対象）、Reddit 2026.44.0（公式の最新の対象・ストアの最新版）、
  SmartNews 26.10.41（Google Play 版の APKM も可）
- 外した版：YouTube 21.20.405・21.42.241、Reddit 2026.24.0・2026.42.0・2026.43.0、SmartNews 26.10.20
  （公式のパッチの対象から外れた版や、新しい版に置き換えた版です）

外した版を使っている場合は、アプリを README の表の版に入れ替えてください。

### YouTube：弾幕

- Morphe 公式のパッチに「Niconico comments」（2.0.0 で追加）が加わりました。これをオンにしている間は、ライブチャットと
  チャットのリプレイをそちらに任せ、同じコメントを二重に流したり、二重に取りに行ったりしないようにしました。
  通常の動画の弾幕はこれまでどおりです。
- 一時停止したり、アプリを閉じたり裏に回したりしたあとも、ライブチャットを取り続けていた問題を直しました。
  再生が 30 秒止まると取得を休み、再生が戻ると最新のコメントから流します。
- コメントがない動画や、コメントが無効の動画で、英語・日本語以外の言語のときに、30 秒ごとにコメントを取り直し
  続けていた問題を直しました。3 回試して見つからなければ止めます。
- 長いライブを見続けると、連投をまとめるための記録が増え続けていた問題を直しました。

### YouTube：プレーヤーのメニュー

- 英語・日本語以外の言語のとき、メニューに弾幕とアンビエントライトの行が出なかった問題を直しました。
- 大きな画面（折りたたみスマホの内側の画面など）で、メニューが歯車の下の小窓で出るとき、弾幕とアンビエントライトの
  行が縦に大きく伸び、小窓の下に余白ができていた問題を直しました。

### Reddit：自動翻訳

- 2026.44.0 で、コメントと投稿の詳細画面が自動で翻訳されなくなっていた問題に対応しました（アプリ側で翻訳の
  ボタンの仕組みが変わったため）。
- 2026.40.0 で、フィードの投稿の一部が自動で翻訳されない問題に対応しました。
- 投稿・コメント・投稿の詳細のどれか 1 つでも仕掛けを入れられない版では、パッチが失敗するようにしました。
  これまでは一部だけ入った状態でも成功していました。

### YouTube：プレーヤーの設定メニュー

- 「弾幕」「アンビエントライト」を、YouTube の「動画のループ再生」などと同じスイッチ付きの行にしました。
  行をタップするとオン・オフが切り替わります。「弾幕・アンビエントライトの設定」の行はなくしました。
- 行を長押しすると、動画の上に小さな設定シートが開きます。オン・オフと、よく使う値（弾幕は文字サイズ・
  不透明度・画面を横切る時間・縦方向の表示範囲、アンビエントライトは明るさ・彩度・なめらかさ）をスライダーで
  変えられ、再生中の動画ですぐに確かめられます。「詳しい設定」からは、これまでの設定画面が開きます。
  初めてオン・オフしたときに、長押しの案内が一度だけ出ます。
- 行の位置・文字の太さ・余白を YouTube の行に合わせ、行の下にできていた空白をなくしました。英語表示の
  ときに「その他」のメニューにも同じ行が重複して出ていたのを、最初のメニューだけにしました。
- 弾幕・アンビエントライトの設定画面から、行の間の区切り線をなくしました（YouTube の設定画面と同じ見た目）。

### YouTube：アンビエントライト

- 動作を軽くしました。これまでは光が変わるたびに、視聴ページや全画面のプレーヤーを描き直していました。
  光を専用の小さな描画面（低い解像度で描き、画面の表示の仕組みが拡大します）に描くようにして、ページや
  プレーヤーは描き直さないようにしました。見た目は変わりません。Android 16 のエミュレーターでは、画面
  全体の描き直しが毎秒約 24 回から約 3 回（全画面では約 1 回）に減り、アンビエントライトをオンにした
  ときのアプリの CPU 使用量が約 1.5〜2 割減りました。
- ほとんど動かない映像（スライドや静止画のような配信）では、映像の取り込みを 1 秒に 5 回まで減らします。
  映像が動くと、すぐ元に戻ります。
- ピクチャー・イン・ピクチャー（小窓）の間とバックグラウンド再生の間は、光の処理を止めます。
- YouTube の「アンビエント モード」と重ならないようにしました。アンビエントライトが表示されている間は
  YouTube 側の効果を隠します。YouTube の設定は変えないので、アンビエントライトをオフにすると元に戻ります。
- 光の見せ方を4つ追加しました。設定画面の「光の見せ方」と、行を長押しして開くシートでオン・オフできます。
  - **背景に動画の映像を映す**（初期値はオフ）：背景を、ぼんやりした色の光ではなく、動画の映像そのものを
    すりガラス越しに見たような表示にします。
  - **画面の下に行くほど暗くする**（初期値はオフ）：プレーヤーのすぐ下がいちばん明るく、画面の下に向かって
    だんだん暗くなります。動画から光がこぼれているように見えます。
  - **場面が変わったら光を広げる**（初期値はオフ）：動画の場面が切り替わったとき、新しい色の光が
    プレーヤーから波のように画面全体へ広がります。
  - **一時停止中は光をゆっくり明滅させる**（初期値はオン）：動画を止めている間、光がゆっくり明るくなったり
    暗くなったりします。電池を少し多く使います。

### YouTube：弾幕

- 「最大フレームレート」を追加しました（詳しい設定の「動きと配置」）。「60fps（電池を節約）」にすると、
  120Hz などの画面でも弾幕を 1 秒に 60 回までしか描かず、画面の書き換えの要求も 60Hz に抑えます。初期値は
  これまでどおり「端末の最大」です。
